{{Short description|Mathematics researcher}}
'''Evans Malott Harrell II''' (born 1950) is an American mathematician known for his research in [[mathematical physics]] and the [[spectral theory]] of [[linear operators]], particularly related to the [[Schrödinger equation]].<ref name=operator/> From 2005 to 2014 he was Professor and Associate Dean in the School of Mathematics at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].<ref name=tech/>

==Early life and education==
Harrell was born in 1950 in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He earned his undergraduate degree from [[Stanford University]] and completed his Ph.D. at [[Princeton University]] in 1976,<ref name=drake/> where his doctoral dissertation was titled "Schrödinger Operators with Singular Perturbation Potentials" under the advisor [[Barry Simon]].<ref name=mgp/> He held visiting and postdoctoral posts at [[Haverford College|Haverford]], the [[University of Vienna]], and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] before his first tenure-track role at [[Johns Hopkins University|Johns Hopkins]]. He joined Georgia Tech in 1983 and remained there until his retirement.<ref name=alumni/>

==Research and Academic Contributions==
Harrell’s research focuses on the analysis of [[differential equation]]s, particularly in the [[spectral theory]] of [[elliptic operator]]s and semiclassical [[quantum mechanics]]. He is recognized for his work on the influence of geometry on the [[eigenvalues and eigenvectors]] of differential equations, as well as for studying the behavior of [[quantum systems]] at atomic scales.<ref name=drake/>

==Education reform==
Harrell has been an active voice in science education reform<ref name=sokal/> and has contributed to international mathematics education. He participated in scientific exchanges and delivered lectures in countries that included [[Benin]], [[Senegal]], and [[Mali]].<ref name=africa/><ref name=alumni/> Additionally, he serves on the board of the educational foundation [[Gathering 4 Gardner]] (G4G).<ref name=G4G/>

==Science Communication through the Arts==
Harrell integrates dance, music, circus arts, and drama into his science communication efforts. He founded Mathematics in Motion, a production company devoted to blending mathematics with the lively arts.<ref name=dance/> Through this initiative, Harrell has produced and directed science-themed performances at various events, including the Atlanta Science Festival<ref name=alumni/> and the [[Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival]].<ref name=tech/>

==Honors==
Harrell won a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1983.<ref name=sloan/> He is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref name=AAAS/> [[Georgia Tech]] awarded him an Outstanding Service Award in 1996 and the Eichholtz Teaching Award in 2006.<ref name=tech/>

==Papers==
* 2016: "[https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.02207 Two-term, asymptotically sharp estimates for eigenvalue means of the Laplacian]" (with  Joachim Stubbe), [[Cornell University]]
* 2009: "[https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/2009-361-05/S0002-9947-08-04780-6/ Universal inequalities for the eigenvalues of Laplace and Schrödinger operators on submanifolds]" (with A El Soufi, E Harrell, S Ilias), Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 361 (5), 2337-2350
* 2003:"[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/1217247 A physical short-channel threshold voltage model for undoped symmetric double-gate MOSFETs]" (with Q Chen and JD Meindl), [[IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices]] 50 (7), 1631-1637
* 2001 "[https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S0036141099357574 On the placement of an obstacle or a well so as to optimize the fundamental eigenvalue]" (with P Kröger & K Kurata) [[SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis]] 33 (1), 240-259
* 1997: "[https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1997-349-05/S0002-9947-97-01846-1/ On trace identities and universal eigenvalue estimates for some partial differential operators]" (with J Stubbe), [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] 349 (5), 1797-1809
* 1994: "[https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03605309408821081 Commutator bounds for eigenvalues, with applications to spectralgeometry] (with PL Michel), Communications in Partial Differential Equations 19 (11-12), 2037-2055
* 1990: "[https://opg.optica.org/ol/abstract.cfm?uri=ol-15-20-1141 Elimination of chaos in an intracavity-doubled Nd: YAG laser]" (with GE James, C Bracikowski, K Wiesenfeld, R Roy), [[Optics Letters]] 15 (20), 1141-1143
* 1990: "[https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.41.2778 Intermittency and chaos in intracavity doubled lasers. II]" (with GE James & R Roy), [[Physical Review]] A 41 (5), 2778
* 1980: "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01212711 Double wells]" [[Communications in Mathematical Physics]] 75 (3), 239-261
* 1980: "[https://projecteuclid.org/journals/duke-mathematical-journal/volume-47/issue-4/The-mathematical-theory-of-resonances-whose-widths-are-exponentially-small/10.1215/S0012-7094-80-04750-X.short The mathematical theory of resonances whose widths are exponentially small]" (with B Simon), Vol. 47, No. 4 [[Duke Mathematical Journal]] (C) December 1980
* 1978: "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01609474 On the rate of asymptotic eigenvalue degeneracy]" Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1), 73-95
